jasper: quick flag - local microbench shows a noticeable p50 regression after the qkv-pack + epilogue merge on short-seq workloads (seq=16). seeing ~7.2% p50 increase on H100 run.
maya: can you drop the bench summary? :eyes:
bench-bot: benchmark run 2026-03-18T14:05Z
bench-bot: model=redwood/fused-attn-next, hw=H100-80GB, batch sizes=1..16, seqs tested=16/64
bench-bot: tokens_per_sec p50: seq16 -> 9.8k (baseline 10.6k), seq64 -> 5.9k (no reg)
bench-bot: p95 latency ms: seq16 -> 5.9ms (baseline 5.4ms)
alex: nvprof excerpt (trimmed):
```
# Kernel timeline (avg per invocation)
fused_qkv_pack_epilogue   us=140.9  regspill=1 shmem=48KB
flash_attn_variant        us=103.4  regspill=0 shmem=32KB
epilogue_cleanup          us=9.7
```
alex: looks like the fused kernel triggers register spills and increased shared-mem usage; impact is amplified when grid size small (bs<=4).
sana: noted similar footprint issues on our earlier H100 runs. Is the epilogue doing rotary, bias, scale, and dropout all inline now? jasper: yes - recent PR consolidated rope+bias+scale into the epilogue to cut launches. PR id: #3190.
liam: does this show up on all head dims? or just narrow ones? alex: mostly when head_dim<=64 and seq small. wider heads and long seqs amortize the extra instructions.
maya: any assembly diffs? alex: simplified asm delta:
```
- fused_epilogue: uses 60 regs, spills 640 bytes per threadblock
+ flash_attn:    uses 44 regs, no spill
```
alex: so spill traffic is non-trivial for tiny grids. plus extra control flow from rope/bias branching.
sana: takeaway: register pressure + ILP drop for short sequences causes latency regression. heavy batching hides it.
ops-bot: canary update - qkv-pack rollout at 12% in prod, monitoring short-prompt customers. observed ~2.8% p50 increase on a small customer subset.
jasper: proposed mitigation experiments (matrix):
- 1) current fused epilogue (control)
- 2) fused minus rope (disable rotary fusion)
- 3) fused minus bias (disable bias fusion)
- 4) split epilogue into two lightweight kernels (compute -> apply)
- 5) force flash-attn path (no fused)
- 6) compile-time low-reg variant: reduce temporaries / hoist to shared mem
liam: also propose runtime chooser policy: if seq<=32 && effective_batch<6 then route to flash-attn fallback. otherwise use fused.
maya: add CI microbench for seq in {8,16,24,32} and bs in {1,2,4,8} so we catch regressions early.
alex: quick sim numbers (from sample corpus) for chooser routing:
bench-bot: - always-fused (serving corpus): tokens/sec ~10.3k
bench-bot: - chooser-smart (small batches -> flash): tokens/sec ~10.9k (+5.8%)
bench-bot: - cost delta: negligible CPU overhead for chooser (~0.15% extra runtime branch cost)
sana: micro-PR suggestions:
- remove per-thread temporaries where possible
- collapse some inline math into precomputed table (small LUT)
- add explicit kernel specializations for head_dim 32/64/128 to reduce generic code paths
jasper: action items:
- @alex run full exp matrix (1..6) and post raw p50/p95 + regcounts (by EOD tomorrow)
- @maya run traffic sim with chooser policy and compute cost per 1M tokens (target 48h)
- @liam prototype runtime chooser flag and add telemetry to opt-in canary (target EOW)
- @sana open perf ticket #3302 with asm diffs and suggested small-PRs
- @ops keep rollout at 12% and pause further expansion until we have mitigations
maya: I have a short-prompt heavy trace. ping me and I9ll hand off the slice.
alex: note: alternative low-effort mitigation: bump dynamic-batching window for short sequences by 1-2ms in the scheduler to increase effective batch and hide spill overhead. tradeoff: slightly higher tail for some interactive traffic.
liam: agree - that9s an ops lever we can test quickly while kernel work proceeds.
jasper: thanks all. unless the 1..6 matrix disproves regspill, plan is to revert rope fusion in the short-seq path and keep it for long sequences. will link PRs once ready.
